question: Can a Neural ODE recover deterministic chaotic vector fields from uniformly sampled, Gaussian-noise-corrupted observations while retaining short-horizon trajectory skill, long-run invariant statistics, manageable training cost, and robustness to a changed numerical solver?

key_findings.claim: Author contribution: WP-NODE combines a local weak residual with only one to five strong-form rollout steps, avoiding numerical differentiation and long backpropagation-through-solver horizons.
key_findings.evidence: Integration by parts turns the ODE residual into integrals of the observed state against a derivative test function and the learned vector field against the test function. Compact polynomial tests phi_p(s)=(1-s^2)^p are shifted over local windows; piecewise-linear quadrature yields precomputable weights. The training objective is L_weak + lambda L_strong with T=2-6, whereas strong baselines use T=25 or 50. Appendix D confirms the vectorized weak term performs standard backpropagation and no ODE integration.

key_findings.claim: Contradiction audit: the paper's filtering explanation is a useful construction and empirical diagnostic, not a general proof that weak-form NODE training recovers the clean vector field.
key_findings.evidence: The equivalence between weak residual targets and a filtered expansion requires an invertible Gram matrix A. The new error discussion additionally assumes smooth f and small noise, approximates f(v)=f(u)+c sigma, and imports a follow-up kernel method's bias-variance analysis; it gives no explicit bias dependence on p, q, and ell. The demonstrated reconstruction uses one Lorenz-63 component at 5% iid Gaussian noise. Thus the evidence supports low-pass behavior under selected local bases, not universal denoising or identifiability of f-dagger.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported parameter diagnostic: a score based only on noisy observations tracks clean-signal reconstruction error on Lorenz-63, while also exposing ill-conditioning and oversmoothing failure modes.
key_findings.evidence: The score averages a target smoothness-ratio penalty and relative one-step persistence error. In the 5% Lorenz-63 sweep, its trend resembles clean RMSE; p=8 is best among tested orders, p=32 makes A ill-conditioned, larger ell averages noise but can erase chaotic features, and q=2 is chosen because q=1 gives only marginal gains at roughly twice as many local intervals. This is a tuned single-system proxy, not a demonstrated universal selection rule.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported Lorenz-63 result: the hybrid is substantially more robust than strong, multistep-penalty, VF-NODE, and DeepSkip baselines as observation noise rises, but pure weak NODE and RAFDA win individual cells.
key_findings.evidence: Across 30 unseen starting points, WP-NODE VPT is 2.90, 2.23, and 0.96 Lyapunov times at 5%, 10%, and 20% noise, versus strong NODE 1.39/0.80/0.36, MP-NODE 0.86/0.45/0.20, VF-NODE 0.86/0.57/0.25, and DeepSkip 0.56/0.34/0.11. WP-NODE KL is 0.002/0.01/0.03. Pure weak NODE has better noiseless VPT and lower 5-10% KL; RAFDA has better 20% VPT. The authors explicitly report that weak-only distribution drift, pointwise-noise amplification, and metric disagreement complicate a single winner claim.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported high-dimensional result: on 40D Lorenz-96, WP-NODE and pure weak NODE are nearly tied and preserve low marginal KL across noise, so the strong penalty adds little demonstrated benefit there.
key_findings.evidence: WP-NODE VPT is 3.65/3.72/3.24/2.75/2.08 from 0-20% noise and weak NODE is 3.66/3.80/3.19/2.71/1.99; both report about 0.02 mean marginal KL throughout. DeepSkip wins VPT at 0-1% but degrades at larger noise. VF-NODE remains about 0.20 VPT and all its long rollouts diverge. The authors caution that near-Gaussian 1D marginals make the KL test insensitive, and the first-four-coordinate KLs vary from 0.010 to 0.042.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported KS result and negative result: WP-NODE gives the best noisy short-term tracking among evaluated methods, but invariant-statistic quality is non-monotonic and can favor a strong NODE.
key_findings.evidence: At 5%, 10%, and 20% noise, WP-NODE VPT is 3.31/2.87/1.53, above strong T=50 at 2.89/2.12/1.27 and weak NODE at 1.97/2.42/0.44. Its KL is excellent at 5% (0.008) but 0.93 with clean data; strong T=25 has lower KL at 0%, 1%, 10%, and 20%. Appendix B states that WP-NODE degrades in the noiseless regime, weak NODE cannot produce stable long runs, and MP-NODE aligns only at 5% noise. The paper attributes the clean-data anomaly to weak quadrature bias and noise acting as implicit regularization.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported solver test: a dopri5-trained WP-NODE preserves the KS joint invariant density under bosh3, Euler, midpoint, and RK4, whereas strong and MP-NODE estimates vary or diverge.
key_findings.evidence: The models are rolled out for 400 seconds, about 20 Lyapunov times, at 5% observation noise. WP-NODE yields visually consistent derivative-space KDEs across all tested integrators; MP-NODE overflows with Euler and midpoint and is truncated, strong NODE changes density by solver, and weak NODE is unstable under all. The result is compelling within one KS discretization but is primarily visual, has no cross-solver numeric table, and does not vary step size or tolerance.

key_findings.claim: Contradiction audit: ERA5 shows bounded long rollouts for the complete WP-NODE recipe, but it does not isolate the weak penalty from architecture and optimization changes or establish competitive weather forecasting.
key_findings.evidence: The experiment replaces the benchmark MLP with an encoder-processor-decoder CNN, T30 preprocessing, latent compression, cylindrical padding, a 12-layer dilated processor, solar forcing, Euler integration, AdamW, mixed precision, and gradient clipping. Comparisons are only weak and strong losses on the same backbone; both baselines diverge while WP-NODE remains bounded for ten years and matches zonal-mean temperature/humidity better than winds. Figures provide curves and climatological profiles but no weather-model baseline, ensemble uncertainty, extreme-event score, conservation metric, or numeric table.

key_findings.claim: Contradiction audit: 'computationally efficient' is accurate per epoch but not as a blanket time-to-train claim on Lorenz-63.
key_findings.evidence: On one A100, WP-NODE T=2 costs 0.077 seconds per epoch versus strong NODE 0.407, weak NODE 0.048, MP-NODE 1.488, and VF-NODE 0.007. Because WP-NODE needs 1,820 epochs, total time is 140 seconds, slower than strong NODE (35 seconds), weak NODE (81), and VF-NODE (131), though much faster than MP-NODE (744). Early-stopping criteria and epoch budgets differ by method, and non-NODE RAFDA/DeepSkip are omitted.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported negative result: a favorably tuned, double-precision VF-NODE fails to scale its global basis to long chaotic records.
key_findings.evidence: The authors reproduce VF-NODE on 10,000-point chaotic Lorenz-63, validate residuals on analytic functions, use double precision, quadruple the default training budget, and sweep smoothing and basis size. The published defaults lambda=0.99 and L_b=80 give VPT below 0.2; at lambda=0.9999, L_b=640 reaches 0.860 but usually diverges long-term. Since global Fourier resolution must grow with total record length, extending it to the 25,000-second KS record is deemed prohibitive. This is the reviewed authors' implementation, not an independently maintained benchmark.

key_findings.claim: Reviewer inference: the defensible novelty is the practical combination of local weak residuals, data-only filter tuning, and a minimal strong rollout, not weak-form learning or noise filtering by itself.
key_findings.evidence: Weak SINDy, variational PINNs, VF-NODE, noisy-data assimilation, and stabilized or multistep NODEs precede the paper; the 2026 WKRR follow-up gives a fuller filter bias-variance account. WP-NODE's distinctive conjunction is local polynomial windows applied directly to raw observations, vectorized solver-free weak loss, and short solver-based supervision, tested on multiple chaotic systems. The evidence does not establish state of the art against all current denoisers, neural operators, weather models, or irregular/sparse sampling methods.

method.core_idea: Use localized weak integral constraints as a noise-filtering, solver-free global consistency term and add only a very short strong-form NODE rollout to restore direct predictive supervision.
method.mechanism: For noisy uniformly spaced observations v_n=u_n+xi_n, integrate the ODE residual against shifted compact polynomial tests and integrate by parts so no derivative of v is needed. Piecewise-linear interpolation yields exact precomputable left and right weights over ell+1 samples, and the vector field network is evaluated independently at all nodes. A reconstruction score based on smoothness and persistence selects p, q, and ell. Training minimizes the vectorized weak residual plus lambda times a T=2-6 rollout MSE. Inference uses an ordinary ODE solver, so the learned vector field can be tested with integrators different from the training solver.
assumptions: The latent dynamics are deterministic; noise enters only through observations and is iid, zero-mean Gaussian with componentwise scale tied to RMS.
Observations are uniformly spaced and dense enough that every local domain contains at least three consecutive points.
The selected local polynomial basis and window resolve the true dynamics without oversmoothing its chaotic features.
The test-function Gram matrix is invertible and sufficiently conditioned for the filtered-expansion interpretation.
The vector field is smooth and observation noise is small enough for the imported first-order filter error argument.
Piecewise-linear quadrature bias is smaller than the noise suppression benefit in the evaluated regime.
Min-max scaling and the same observed state used as a rollout initial condition do not introduce a material train-test mismatch.
VPT and marginal or derivative-space KL jointly capture the relevant short- and long-run behavior of each chaotic system.
The chosen baseline implementations, budgets, precision, hyperparameter sweeps, and early-stopping rules are sufficiently comparable.
The ERA5 reanalysis trajectory can be treated as samples of a deterministic conditioned ODE despite unresolved stochasticity and model error.
A bounded ten-year Euler rollout and zonal climatology imply useful learned climate dynamics rather than only numerical damping.
Solver agreement on one KS rollout indicates approximation of a continuous vector field rather than coincident stability across those settings.

techniques.role: Projects the ODE residual onto compact tests so integrated constraints average high-frequency observation noise.
Moves the time derivative from the unknown clean trajectory to the known test function.
Expresses each local integral as batched dot products with precomputed polynomial antiderivative weights.
Chooses polynomial order, spacing, and support using smoothness and persistence diagnostics without clean labels.
Adds one to five rollout steps to a solver-free weak loss to trade integrated consistency for local forecast fidelity.
Measures the first time normalized trajectory error crosses a system-specific threshold.
Uses 1D marginal KDEs for Lorenz systems and a 2D derivative-space KDE for KS to assess long-run statistics.
Runs a dopri5-trained vector field with adaptive and fixed-step solvers to probe discretization overfitting.
Extends the loss to four ERA5 fields with cylindrical convolutions, solar conditioning, and Euler integration.
Sweeps VF-NODE smoothing and basis resolution on a long chaotic record to expose global-basis scaling.

evaluations.setting: 5% noisy Lorenz-63 signal and vector-field reconstruction
evaluations.metric: Clean-signal RMSE and noisy-data composite score J over p, q, ell
evaluations.result: p=8, q=2, ell=50 filters below the observation-noise scale; p=32 amplifies error through an ill-conditioned Gram matrix and large windows risk oversmoothing.
evaluations.baseline: Raw noisy observation and alternate polynomial orders, spacings, and supports

evaluations.metric: VPT in Lyapunov times and 100-second marginal-KDE KL divergence
evaluations.result: WP-NODE leads the NODE family under noisy conditions and has VPT 2.90/2.23/0.96 with KL 0.002/0.01/0.03 at 5/10/20% noise.
evaluations.baseline: Strong, weak, MP-NODE, tuned VF-NODE, DeepSkip, and RAFDA; pure weak or RAFDA win selected cells

evaluations.metric: VPT and mean 1D marginal-KDE KL divergence
evaluations.result: WP-NODE and weak NODE remain nearly tied, with WP-NODE VPT 2.08 and KL 0.02 at 20% noise; VF-NODE long runs diverge at every level.
evaluations.baseline: Strong, weak, MP-NODE, VF-NODE, and DeepSkip; marginal KL has limited sensitivity here

evaluations.result: WP-NODE has the best noisy VPT among evaluated methods and KL 0.008 at 5%, but its clean KL is 0.93 and strong T=25 wins several KL cells.
evaluations.baseline: Strong NODE T=25 and 50, weak NODE, MP-NODE, and DeepSkip

evaluations.setting: KS, 400-second rollout after dopri5 training at 5% noise
evaluations.metric: Visual consistency of derivative-space invariant densities across bosh3, Euler, midpoint, RK4, and dopri5
evaluations.result: WP-NODE remains consistent; strong changes by solver, weak is unstable, and MP-NODE overflows under Euler and midpoint.
evaluations.baseline: Strong NODE, weak NODE, and MP-NODE under the same solver switch; no numeric cross-solver score

evaluations.metric: VPT and KL while varying p, ell, q, T, lambda, batch, depth, and sample count
evaluations.result: p=8, ell=50, q=2, T=2, lambda=0.5, batch 2048, and two hidden layers are selected, but VPT-optimal choices do not always minimize KL.
evaluations.baseline: One-at-a-time parameter alternatives without interaction analysis or repeated-run uncertainty

evaluations.setting: L63 wall-clock benchmark on one NVIDIA A100
evaluations.metric: Seconds per epoch, epochs to stopping, and total seconds
evaluations.result: WP-NODE is 0.077 s/epoch and 140 s total, versus strong 0.407/35, weak 0.048/81, MP-NODE 1.488/744, and VF-NODE 0.007/131.
evaluations.baseline: NODE variants with method-specific budgets and stopping rules

evaluations.setting: ERA5 T30 four-field reanalysis with 7.9 years training data
evaluations.metric: 6-hour/24-hour and 14-day RMSE curves, bounded 10-year rollout, and zonal climatological profiles
evaluations.result: WP-NODE stays bounded and has lower plotted error than weak and strong NODE; temperature and humidity climatology align better than wind fields.
evaluations.baseline: Weak and strong loss on the same CNN only; no operational forecast, neural weather, persistence, or climatology baseline

evaluations.setting: VF-NODE reproduction on 10,000-point chaotic Lorenz-63 at 5% noise
evaluations.metric: VPT, bounded long-run KL, epoch time, and sensitivity to spline lambda and L_b
evaluations.result: Defaults fail below 0.2 VPT; tuned lambda=0.9999 and L_b=640 reaches 0.860 VPT but generally diverges long-term and loses its scaling advantage.
evaluations.baseline: Published VF-NODE defaults and WP-NODE's local basis; reproduction is by the reviewed authors

limitations: Author-stated: the current quadrature assumes uniform spacing; dense observations are required and isolated snapshot pairs or large temporal gaps are unsupported.
Author-stated: weak-only training can have short-horizon skill but drift to the wrong invariant distribution because it has no rollout supervision.
Author-stated: p, q, ell, T, lambda, batch size, and architecture create VPT-versus-KL trade-offs rather than a single universally best setting.
Author-stated: RAFDA is omitted above Lorenz-63 because the tested implementation exceeds 24 hours without localization and inflation tuning.
Author-stated: VF-NODE is not extended to KS because global basis size must grow with record length and the global integral cannot be minibatched.
Author-stated: ERA5 wind climatologies retain deviations even when thermodynamic variables are captured better.
Reviewer-inferred: the iid Gaussian observation model excludes colored, state-dependent, missing, irregular, and process noise common in sensors and climate data.
Reviewer-inferred: the filter argument depends on Gram invertibility, small noise, smooth f, and a single Lorenz reconstruction; no recovery theorem is proved for the neural estimator.
Reviewer-inferred: baseline budgets, stopping criteria, rollout horizons, precision, and hyperparameter effort are not fully matched.
Reviewer-inferred: VPT and low-dimensional marginal KL can miss phase, cross-coordinate, spectral, conservation, and rare-event errors.
Reviewer-inferred: the ERA5 experiment changes backbone, optimizer, padding, forcing, solver, and precision and reports no numeric table or competitive weather baseline.
Reviewer-inferred: most results are point estimates without seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, code release, or an independent reproduction.
Reviewer-inferred: solver robustness is assessed visually on one KS model without a step-size or tolerance sweep.
Reviewer-inferred: a ten-year bounded climate rollout can arise from excessive damping and does not by itself establish useful forecast dynamics.
failure_modes: High polynomial order can make the test-function Gram system ill-conditioned and amplify rather than remove noise.
Large integration support can erase fast chaotic modes, while short support averages too little noise.
Quadrature bias can dominate on clean data, producing the observed poor KS invariant measure for WP-NODE at 0% noise.
A short strong target is itself noisy; its benefit can disappear when pointwise corruption grows faster than weak quadrature error.
Sparse, irregular, gappy, asynchronous, or event-based observations violate the implemented window and weight construction.
Process noise or stochastic dynamics can be mistaken for observation error and filtered out of the learned vector field.
Weak-only fits can satisfy local moments yet generate unstable or distribution-shifted long rollouts.
Strong and penalty NODEs can encode a particular integrator's truncation behavior and fail when solver or step changes.
Marginal KL can look good for near-Gaussian L96 coordinates even when joint attractor geometry is wrong.
VPT can be low despite visually useful forecasts or high despite a wrong invariant distribution, so optimizing either metric can misselect models.
ERA5 Euler training may favor an artificially dissipative vector field that is bounded but weak on transients, extremes, and winds.
Global Fourier variational bases can become computationally infeasible as the training interval grows, whereas local bases still incur many overlapping segments.
Min-max scaling can distort rare amplitudes and make out-of-range rollouts unstable.
The method may fail when vector-field architecture error, not observation noise, is the dominant source of residual.
reusable_insights: Pair a solver-free integral residual with a very short rollout rather than differentiating through a long chaotic trajectory.
Move derivatives onto analytic test functions before learning from noisy state observations.
Use compact support when record length is large so resolution and minibatching do not scale with the global horizon.
Precompute weak quadrature weights and express the loss as batched dot products for memory-efficient training.
Select denoising windows from observables such as residual whiteness, smoothness, and persistence, then separately validate dynamics.
Audit short-run trajectory skill and long-run invariant structure independently because their optima can disagree.
Include clean-data tests: noise can regularize quadrature bias and hide a method's baseline approximation error.
Test a learned continuous vector field under several integrators, step sizes, and tolerances to detect discretization overfitting.
Report per-epoch and time-to-target costs; vectorized objectives may require many more epochs.
Match precision, budgets, stopping, parameter counts, and hyperparameter searches when benchmarking scientific-learning methods.
For climate surrogates, distinguish boundedness from accuracy with spectra, conservation, extremes, anomaly correlations, and operational baselines.
Treat weak-loss design as a bias-variance problem: basis count, support, spacing, and quadrature jointly determine both terms.
open_questions: Can one prove finite-sample vector-field recovery or forecast error bounds for WP-NODE under explicit basis, network, quadrature, and noise assumptions?
How do the optimal p, q, ell, and lambda scale with sampling rate, Lyapunov spectrum, noise color, and state dimension?
Can adaptive or learned test functions preserve fast modes while suppressing state-dependent and colored noise?
How should the method handle irregular times, missing intervals, multirate sensors, and isolated snapshot pairs without biased interpolation?
Does the hybrid remain robust under process noise or genuinely stochastic latent dynamics?
Which component causes solver transfer: local weak constraints, short rollouts, or their interaction in a matched ablation?
Does cross-solver robustness persist across step-size and tolerance grids and for stiff or multiscale systems?
Would joint, spectral, Wasserstein, topological, and conservation metrics reverse conclusions based on marginal KL?
How does WP-NODE compare with current weak kernel methods, neural operators, score-based denoisers, and state-space models under matched compute?
Can the ERA5 result reproduce against persistence, climatology, numerical forecasts, and modern neural weather models on standard forecast scores?
Is the ten-year ERA5 rollout dynamically correct or merely bounded through excess numerical and architectural dissipation?
Can uncertainty quantification distinguish observation noise, model misspecification, and chaotic sensitivity in learned rollouts?
Will an independent implementation reproduce the tuned VF-NODE failure and the reported WP-NODE noise crossover?

competitive_landscape.title: Accelerating Neural ODEs: A Variational Formulation-based Approach
competitive_landscape.difference: VF-NODE removes solver integration through global Fourier-sine tests, natural-cubic-spline preprocessing, and Filon quadrature. WP-NODE instead uses raw local polynomial windows plus a short strong rollout; its current paper supplies an author-run chaotic-regime stress test in which VF-NODE's basis must grow with record length.
competitive_landscape.source_version: ICLR 2025 conference paper, OpenReview forum trV41CpAK4

competitive_landscape.title: Divide and conquer: Learning chaotic dynamical systems with multistep penalty neural ordinary differential equations
competitive_landscape.difference: MP-NODE splits long chaotic trajectories and penalizes discontinuities to control exploding gradients while retaining solver rollouts. WP-NODE replaces most sequential simulation with local integral constraints, is much cheaper per epoch, and targets observation-noise robustness; MP-NODE remains architecture-agnostic but is expensive and solver-sensitive in the reported KS test.

competitive_landscape.title: Stabilized neural ordinary differential equations for long-time forecasting of dynamical systems
competitive_landscape.difference: Stabilized NODE builds a learned dissipative linear term plus nonlinear network into the vector field and demonstrates KS attractor stability and noisy-initial-condition robustness. WP-NODE changes the training loss rather than imposing that architecture and addresses noisy training observations, but does not compare directly to this strong structural baseline.

competitive_landscape.title: Weak SINDy for partial differential equations
competitive_landscape.difference: WSINDy uses compact convolutional weak forms, FFT acceleration, spectral test selection, and sparse regression to recover interpretable PDE terms under heavy noise. WP-NODE removes the predefined dictionary restriction and focuses on black-box forecasting, sacrificing equation sparsity and interpretability while adding short rollout supervision.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning dynamical systems with hit-and-run random feature maps
competitive_landscape.difference: DeepSkip learns fixed-step tendency maps with hit-and-run features, skip connections, depth, and localization, achieving strong clean L63/L96/KS forecasts cheaply. Its version-of-record experiments explicitly assume complete noise-free observations; WP-NODE is continuous-time and robust to corrupted training data but loses badly to DeepSkip in several clean VPT cells.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning dynamical systems from noisy data with Weak-form Kernel Ridge Regression
competitive_landscape.difference: WKRR gives the weak filter a kernel ridge estimator and a more explicit bias-variance decomposition, with experiments through 64D chaos and 15,000D fluid data. WP-NODE predates it and offers flexible neural vector fields plus short rollout supervision; after this follow-up, filtering itself and its bias-variance interpretation are no longer distinctive novelty.

competitive_landscape.title: Supervised learning from noisy observations: Combining machine-learning techniques with data assimilation
competitive_landscape.difference: RAFDA couples random-feature learning with an ensemble Kalman filter and is highly robust on noisy Lorenz-63, including better 20% VPT than WP-NODE. WP-NODE avoids ensemble filtering and scales to larger reported states, while the evaluated RAFDA implementation becomes impractical without localization and inflation engineering.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural ODEs with Irregular and Noisy Data
competitive_landscape.relationship: noisy and irregular Neural ODE precursor
competitive_landscape.difference: Goyal and Benner directly study Neural ODE training when observations are noisy and irregular. WP-NODE contributes a local weak-plus-short-strong objective and stronger chaotic-system tests, but its implemented quadrature gives up irregular and sparse timing support that this precursor targets.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv:2205.09479v1, submitted 2022-05-19; later published as DOI 10.1098/rsos.221475

novelty_assessment.author_claim: A properly parameterized local weak formulation filters noisy observations, and using it as a penalty beside a short strong NODE loss yields computationally efficient, solver-agnostic, accurate short-term and invariant-statistical forecasts across chaotic benchmarks and ERA5.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper constructs local polynomial weak quadrature, a data-only filter score, L63/L96/KS noise sweeps with VPT and KL, hyperparameter and wall-clock analyses, a cross-integrator KS test, ten-year ERA5 rollouts, and a favorable chaotic-regime reproduction of global-basis VF-NODE.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The strongest novelty is the specific engineering synthesis of locally supported raw-data weak residuals, observable-only basis tuning, and one-to-five-step rollout supervision. Weak-form denoising, weak SINDy, variational NODEs, data assimilation, stable NODE architectures, and penalty shooting all precede it, and a same-group 2026 WKRR paper gives a stronger filter analysis. Claims of general state of the art, computational efficiency, and real-world climate fidelity should be narrowed: individual baselines win clean or long-run cells, total training time is not best, assumptions exclude irregular/process noise, and ERA5 lacks competitive forecast baselines and controlled isolation.

reviewer_notes: All 31 physical pages of the hash-pinned extraction were read, including every main table, floating full-page figure, Appendices A-E, quadrature derivations, negative cells, and the new VF-NODE reproduction. The pinned PDF is arXiv v5, which the official arXiv record lists as revised 2026-08-17; this matters because earlier HTML snapshots omit Appendix E and several caveats. Eight direct official primary competitor records were checked at their exact current versions on 2026-08-23. Claims are separated from reviewer inference; the principal audit risks are unmatched baseline effort, the heuristic filter-to-recovery step, clean-data quadrature bias, insensitive marginal KL, and ERA5 architecture/evaluation confounds.
